rationale.conceptual: The method involves an established, multi-part protocol (equation-of-state fitting, volume-conserving strain for elastic constants, Voigt-Reuss-Hill averaging, quasi-harmonic Debye model) that requires non-trivial understanding and careful implementation, but it is a standard application of DFT rather than a novel derivation or custom algorithm.
rationale.execution: The pipeline has four sequential stages with dependencies (structural → elastic → derived moduli → thermodynamics). Executing it entails many individual DFT calculations (energy-volume scans, strain distortions) and subsequent data processing, but the orchestration is not overly fragile or lengthy; a competent researcher can automate the workflow without exceptional engineering challenges.

difficulty.reasoning: The paper applies standard DFT calculations (energy-volume scans, elastic constants via strain) and a quasi-harmonic Debye model to predict properties of HoAs and HoP. The method is a well-established workflow in computational materials science, requiring careful implementation of several sequential steps but no novel algorithms. Execution involves managing multiple DFT runs and data post-processing, which is moderate in complexity. Resource needs are modest (CPU-only plane-wave calculations on small unit cells).

compute_estimate.reasoning: Plane-wave DFT on small (2-atom) rocksalt unit cells with moderate cutoff (~500 eV) and k-point mesh (12×12×12); no phonon supercell calculations are required. The entire workload runs on a standard CPU cluster or even a powerful workstation with a few dozen GB of RAM, and input data consists only of atomic positions and pseudopotentials.
